neutral_facts.correct_value: The proprietor of a multi-storied hotel and adjoining club in Indore obtained a building permission in 1993, valid for one year, with renewal required before a set date. A revised building plan was later submitted to the Building Officer, who approved it along with a renewal of the permission, and a completion certificate for the adjoining club was granted shortly afterwards. The prosecution alleged that the revised plan was a complete departure from the original plan, with the built-up area of the hotel increased substantially and that of the club's ground floor decreased markedly. It was alleged that the revision was sanctioned without approval from the high-rise building committee and without electricity, water supply, sewage and fire-safety clearances. It was further alleged that the completion certificate was issued only seven days after the revision of the permission, although the club could not plausibly have been completed with all compliances within that time. A Sub-Engineer in the building permission branch was alleged to have made notings in the note sheet favouring the proprietor. It was alleged that the Building Officer received free lifetime honorary membership of the club for the officer and five family members as illegal gratification. The Building Officer was also alleged to have failed to inform the property tax department about the completion certificate, leading to alleged tax evasion of Rs.5,49,000. An anti-corruption agency registered a first information report in January 1998 and, after investigation, filed a charge-sheet against the three accused.
